result:
The API keys table now has a Last used column and a Rotate button on every row. I didn't run tests, lint, `pnpm i18n` or the app, so none of it has been checked.

**Last used column**
- The list query now also reads `lastUsedAt`.
- The column shows a relative time, or "Never used" when the key hasn't been used. It reuses the existing `common.last_used` label.
- I narrowed the widths of the other columns so the new one fits. `loading.tsx` also builds its columns from the same factory, so I updated it too.

**Rotate**
- Clicking Rotate opens a confirmation dialog. It warns that the current key stops working right away.
- On confirm, the key keeps its label, organization access and workspace permissions, and gets a new secret. Its last used time resets to "Never used".
- The new key appears in the key column with the copy icon, the same way a freshly created key does. It is gone after a page reload.
- The server action rule in `apps/web/AGENTS.md` meant I couldn't add one, so rotate is a new session-only route, `POST /api/internal/api-keys/{apiKeyId}/rotate`. I put it under `/api/internal` rather than `/api/v3`, because nothing outside the app calls it and `/api/v3` would have required spec work.
- The route requires the same `apiKey.manage` permission as delete and edit. It also refuses to rotate a key with organization write access unless the caller could grant that access today, matching the check used when creating a key.
- The new secret is never written to the audit log.
- I added a small TanStack Query provider around the table, because the page had none.

**Still to do**
- I only added the new strings to `en-US.json`. Run `pnpm i18n` to generate the other locales.
- I didn't add tests, so rotate has none. The standards call for a unit test on the route, like the reactivate route's `route.test.ts`.

The main change is in `apps/web/modules/organization/settings/api-keys/components/edit-api-keys.tsx`. The route is under `apps/web/app/api/internal/api-keys/[apiKeyId]/rotate/`.
